title: Water Polo: training overview
d: Water Polo training builds the fitness, skills, and tactics the rules demand.
definition: Water Polo training builds the fitness, skills, and tactics the rules demand.
description: Water Polo training has three pillars: the physical engine, the technical skills, and the tactical brain. The rules define the demands — 7 per side (6 + goalie) over four 8-minute periods of actual play — and training reverses them into a program: energy systems for the duration, strength for the collisions and jumps, skills for the techniques, tactics for the decisions. This database covers all four across a season, from first preseason week to championship taper.

d: Water Polo runs on: Court-team sports demand lateral quickness and jump repeatability within four 8-minute periods of actual play. Short-burst conditioning with incomplete rest mirrors the game..

Short-burst conditioning with incomplete rest mirrors the game. Match the conditioning to the clock — train the exact work-to-rest ratios the sport uses, because fitness is specific. Test the systems with time trials and heart-rate data, then target the weakest one first; the fittest athlete is rarely the winner, but the unfittest never is.

title: Strength program
d: Water Polo strength work: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder..
definition: Water Polo strength work: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder..
description: Strength training for Water Polo: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder. Train strength twice a week in season, three times out of it. Lift for the sport, not for the mirror — every exercise should answer which on-field action it improves. Keep a training log; progressive overload over months is what separates good from great.

title: Conditioning plan
d: Water Polo conditioning mirrors four 8-minute periods of actual play: work-to-rest matched to the game clock.
definition: Water Polo conditioning mirrors four 8-minute periods of actual play: work-to-rest matched to the game clock.
description: Conditioning for Water Polo must mirror the game clock: four 8-minute periods of actual play. Build the aerobic base first — it speeds recovery between hard efforts — then layer sport-specific intervals. Never sacrifice skill sessions for extra running; tired athletes learn bad technique. Monitor with resting heart rate and repeat-sprint tests.

title: Skill acquisition
d: Learn Water Polo skills in three stages: grooved, pressured, then match-random.
definition: Learn Water Polo skills in three stages: grooved, pressured, then match-random.
description: Skill learning in Water Polo follows blocked-to-random progression: first groove the movement alone, then add pressure, then randomize like a match. Ten thousand mindless reps engrave errors; one thousand deliberate reps with feedback engrave skill. Film everything — athletes cannot fix what they cannot see.

title: Tactical training
d: Water Polo tactics are rehearsed, not improvised: walk, jog, full speed, then live.
definition: Water Polo tactics are rehearsed, not improvised: walk, jog, full speed, then live.
description: Tactical training in Water Polo: walk through the shape, jog it, run it full speed, then go live. Tactics fail when players think instead of recognize — so rehearse until recognition is instant. Review film weekly: pause at decisions and ask what the right choice was before revealing it.

title: Sports nutrition
d: Fuel Water Polo: carbs for the work, protein for repair, timing around sessions.
definition: Fuel Water Polo: carbs for the work, protein for repair, timing around sessions.
description: Nutrition for Water Polo athletes: carbohydrate covers the training load, protein (about 1.6-2.2 g per kg daily) repairs it, and fluids with electrolytes cover the sweat. Eat a familiar meal 3 hours before competition and a carb-protein mix within 2 hours after. Supplements are the last one percent — food is the other ninety-nine.

title: Hydration plan
d: Water Polo hydration: start hydrated, drink to thirst plus plan, replace after.
definition: Water Polo hydration: start hydrated, drink to thirst plus plan, replace after.
description: Hydration for Water Polo: weigh before and after sessions to learn your sweat rate, drink on a schedule in long events, and replace sodium in heat. Losing two percent of body mass to dehydration measurably impairs skill and decisions. Practice the race-day drinking plan in training — never try anything new on competition day.

title: Recovery methods
d: Recover from Water Polo: sleep first, then easy movement, food, and stress control.
definition: Recover from Water Polo: sleep first, then easy movement, food, and stress control.
description: Recovery from Water Polo training ranks: sleep (8-9 hours for athletes) first, then light movement, then nutrition timing, then stress management. Ice baths and gadgets are minor compared to sleep. Track morning readiness — soreness, mood, resting heart rate — and adjust the day's load to it.

title: Sleep for athletes
d: Water Polo athletes need 8-9 hours: sleep is when training adaptations happen.
definition: Water Polo athletes need 8-9 hours: sleep is when training adaptations happen.
description: Sleep is the legal performance enhancer for Water Polo: growth hormone peaks in deep sleep, skills consolidate overnight, and reaction time degrades measurably with debt. Keep the room cool, dark, and screen-free; keep wake time consistent even on weekends. Naps of 20-30 minutes help; long late naps hurt night sleep.

title: Mental skills
d: Train the Water Polo mind: routines, self-talk, visualization, and pressure rehearsal.
definition: Train the Water Polo mind: routines, self-talk, visualization, and pressure rehearsal.
description: Mental training for Water Polo: a pre-performance routine that never changes, self-talk that is instructional not emotional, visualization of successful execution, and deliberate pressure practice. Confidence comes from preparation evidence — keep a log of good sessions to read before big events. Anxiety is normal; unmanaged anxiety is optional.

title: Season planning
d: Plan the Water Polo year: base, build, peak, and transition phases.
definition: Plan the Water Polo year: base, build, peak, and transition phases.
description: Season planning for Water Polo runs in phases: base (volume and technique), build (intensity and tactics), peak (sharpen for championships), transition (rest and play). One peak per season for most athletes; trying to peak year-round peaks never. Schedule deload weeks every 3-4 weeks — adaptation happens in recovery.

title: Tapering
d: Taper for Water Polo championships: cut volume 40-60%, keep intensity sharp.
definition: Taper for Water Polo championships: cut volume 40-60%, keep intensity sharp.
description: The Water Polo taper: 1-3 weeks out, cut training volume by 40 to 60 percent but keep some sharp intensity so the body stays awake. Sleep more, eat familiar food, trust the training. Most athletes taper too little and arrive flat, or train through and arrive tired — the taper is part of the program, not time off.

title: Youth development
d: Young Water Polo athletes: sample many sports, prioritize fun and fundamentals.
definition: Young Water Polo athletes: sample many sports, prioritize fun and fundamentals.
description: Youth Water Polo development: before age 14, multi-sport sampling beats early specialization for both skill and health. Keep sessions short, playful, and technique-rich; measure success in smiles and improvement, not trophies. Never year-round single-sport training before puberty — overuse injuries end more careers than opponents do.

title: Injury prevention
d: Prevent Water Polo injuries: warm up, strengthen the known weak links, manage load.
definition: Prevent Water Polo injuries: warm up, strengthen the known weak links, manage load.
description: Injury prevention in Water Polo targets the sport's known patterns: structured warm-ups (like FIFA 11+ style programs) cut injuries measurably, strength work protects joints, and load management — never spiking weekly volume more than about ten percent — prevents most overuse injuries. Report pain early; playing through sharp pain turns small problems into seasons lost.

title: Fitness testing
d: Test Water Polo fitness: repeat the same battery every 6-8 weeks.
definition: Test Water Polo fitness: repeat the same battery every 6-8 weeks.
description: Fitness testing for Water Polo: pick 4-6 tests covering speed, endurance, power, and sport skill, and repeat the identical battery every 6-8 weeks. Tests direct the program — train the weakest result. Record everything; athletes who test improve faster because the numbers make progress visible.

title: Return to play
d: Return to Water Polo after injury: criteria-based, not calendar-based.
definition: Return to Water Polo after injury: criteria-based, not calendar-based.
description: Return to Water Polo after injury follows criteria, not dates: full range of motion, strength symmetry, sport-specific movements pain-free, then controlled contact, then full training, then competition. Rushing back re-injures; the second injury is usually worse. Clearance from a clinician plus passing functional tests is the standard.

title: Pre-game routine
d: Water Polo pre-game: same timeline, same warm-up, same mindset every time.
definition: Water Polo pre-game: same timeline, same warm-up, same mindset every time.
description: The Water Polo pre-game routine: fixed timeline from arrival, dynamic warm-up progressing to sport speed, equipment check, tactical reminders, then quiet focus. Routines calm nerves by making the unfamiliar familiar. Rehearse the routine before minor events so it is automatic for major ones.

title: Video analysis
d: Study Water Polo film: your reps, opponents' tendencies, and elite models.
definition: Study Water Polo film: your reps, opponents' tendencies, and elite models.
description: Video analysis in Water Polo: review your own reps first (technique), then opponents (tendencies), then elite models (what great looks like). Keep clips short and specific — three clips with one fix each beats an hour of passive watching. Athletes who study film make better decisions under pressure.

title: Goal setting
d: Set Water Polo goals in three layers: outcome, performance, and process.
definition: Set Water Polo goals in three layers: outcome, performance, and process.
description: Goal setting for Water Polo: outcome goals (win the league) motivate, performance goals (improve first-touch success) direct, and process goals (today's drill focus) control the day. Write them down, review weekly, and keep process goals in the majority — athletes control effort and execution, not scoreboards.

title: Cross-training
d: Cross-train for Water Polo: swim, bike, or lift to build fitness without sport load.
definition: Cross-train for Water Polo: swim, bike, or lift to build fitness without sport load.
description: Cross-training for Water Polo keeps fitness growing while the sport-specific tissues rest: swimming for cardio without impact, cycling for legs without pounding, strength work for armor. One cross session weekly in season, more in the off-season. Variety also refreshes the mind — burnout ends more seasons than injuries do.

title: Equipment care
d: Water Polo gear lasts longer and performs better with basic maintenance.
definition: Water Polo gear lasts longer and performs better with basic maintenance.
description: Equipment care in Water Polo: clean it, dry it, store it right, and inspect it before every session. Worn gear causes injuries — dead shoes, frayed ropes, cracked helmets retire on schedule, not after failure. Keep a spare of anything that would end your day if it broke.

title: Travel competition
d: Travel for Water Polo events: control what you can — sleep, food, and warm-up.
definition: Travel for Water Polo events: control what you can — sleep, food, and warm-up.
description: Travel competition in Water Polo: arrive as early as the budget allows, bring familiar food, protect sleep across time zones, and scout the venue on arrival. Keep the pre-game routine identical to home — familiarity is calming. Pack backups of every critical item in carry-on.

title: Off-season
d: The Water Polo off-season: rest first, then rebuild the base and fix weaknesses.
definition: The Water Polo off-season: rest first, then rebuild the base and fix weaknesses.
description: The Water Polo off-season has two halves: complete rest for 2-4 weeks (mental and physical), then base rebuilding with high volume and low pressure. Fix the weakest link identified in testing, try a new sport for athleticism, and return to preseason hungry. Athletes who skip the off-season borrow from next year.
